instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. The task must be completed through an interactive graphical workflow. Use the the selected finite-element tool the graphical analysis environment GUI to complete a linear eigenvalue buckling analysis. Physical problem: A pin-ended straight column is subjected to axial compression. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use the global Cartesian coordinate system. - Model the column as a line body with a beam cross-section. - The column axis is along the global Y direction. - The bottom end is located at Y = 0 mm. - The top end is located at Y = 1000 mm. - The rectangular beam section is: - Width = 10 mm - Height = 10 mm Model parameters: - Line body length: 1000 mm - Section type: rectangular beam section - Section size: 10 mm × 10 mm - Material: Structural Steel with the following linear elastic properties: - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3 - Use a consistent N-mm unit system. Boundary conditions: - Bottom end at Y = 0 mm: - Constrain UX = 0, UY = 0, and UZ = 0. - Leave all rotations free. - Top end at Y = 1000 mm: - Constrain UX = 0 and UZ = 0. - Leave UY free. - Leave all rotations free. - Apply an axial compressive reference load of 1 N at the top end in the negative global Y direction. Analysis type: - Linear eigenvalue buckling analysis. - Extract the first buckling mode. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop.
